presentation_contract: Party identifiers and names are masked in the public application; event references remain traceable.
human_decision_boundary: Only an authorized human investigator may close a case, escalate enhanced due diligence, or recommend a regulatory filing. This repository records no such approval or filing.

typologies.hypothesis: Repeated cash deposits may be deliberately kept below a reporting threshold.
typologies.lawful_lookalike: Cash-intensive retail activity with regular till deposits.
typologies.discriminator: Source of funds, deposit cadence, business receipts and related-account activity.
typologies.known_limitation: A fixed seven-day window can miss deposits that are both thinned and spread.

typologies.hypothesis: A large inbound transfer may be rapidly dispersed to several counterparties.
typologies.lawful_lookalike: Wholesale settlement followed by a scheduled supplier-payment batch.
typologies.discriminator: Invoice support, counterparty purpose, retained balance and relationship history.
typologies.known_limitation: The single-institution view cannot observe the next hop after funds leave.

typologies.hypothesis: Many small inbound transfers from distinct senders may represent coordinated collection.
typologies.lawful_lookalike: Marketplace, fundraising or event receipts from many unrelated customers.
typologies.discriminator: Sender relationships, stated account purpose, campaign evidence and withdrawal behaviour.
typologies.known_limitation: Shared counterparties do not by themselves establish coordination.

typologies.hypothesis: Large round-dollar payments may be inconsistent with the entity's normal distribution.
typologies.lawful_lookalike: Rent, payroll, tax, treasury or contract milestone payments.
typologies.discriminator: Payment purpose, agreement or invoice, recurrence and entity-specific baseline.
typologies.known_limitation: Roundness is weak evidence unless it is evaluated relative to the entity.

typologies.hypothesis: Material activity after a long dormant period may indicate account takeover or repurposing.
typologies.lawful_lookalike: Seasonal use, a matured investment or a legitimate one-off purchase.
typologies.discriminator: Authentication events, customer contact, source of funds and historical purpose.
typologies.known_limitation: Only the first transaction after dormancy should trigger the rule.
